elements.evidence: "commercial general liability insurance ... of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence"
"professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000"

elements.evidence: "Array shall maintain, at its own expense"
"professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000"
"cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000"

reasons: The inserted Section 18.15 expressly delivers every preferred element: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M conditioned on Array's processing of Ono confidential/personal data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates on request.
Obligation is placed on the Vendor (Array) at its own expense, with the Customer (Ono) as beneficiary, so party direction is correct.

The Agreement had no insurance covenant at all; a single concise new section is the minimal way to complete the level, and no existing sentence (16.4, 16.5, 18.14) was altered, so unrelated commercial terms remain effective.

Ancillary qualifiers ('including product liability and contractual liability coverage'; 'and for one (1) year thereafter') are customary scope wording within a short insertion and do not create undefined terms, contradictions, or dangling mechanics; they favour our side and are noted rather than treated as bargaining overreach.
Fallback amounts are also satisfied on the face of the drafted minimums, but the clause stands at the locked preferred level; classification is compliant and no further redline is warranted.
